newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds flat to higher, eye U.S. jobless.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds flat to higher, eye U.S. jobless.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to higher Wednesday as the market maintained a firm tone although some worries set in ahead of the release Friday of the U.S. jobless report.
"The market is reaccommodating itself slowly, with slight gains, which shows the market is still firm and investors are reluctant about leaving their positions," said an analyst.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 93-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was flat at 116.80.
"There is some uncertainy surrounding the announcement of U.S. unemployment, which may give an idea of future monetary policy," said a trader.
Otherwise, the market got more uplifting economic news on the home front Wednesday, with the announcement of gross domestic product growth of 8.1 percent in the first quarter.
The Economy Ministry also said it had revised 1996 growth to 4.3 percent from 4.4 percent.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.78 percent.
